messages:
alina (People Ops): Quick question for the policy thread  are laundry/dry-cleaning expenses reimbursable on trips longer than 7 nights? Someone flagged a $65 dry-cleaning charge on a 10-night client trip.

people-ops-bot: Policy excerpt: "Incidental services (e.g., laundry, dry-cleaning) may be reimbursed on business trips longer than 7 consecutive nights. Receipts required. Limit: US$75 per 7-night period unless pre-approved."

rachel (Engineering): I assumed per diem covers small things like that. We charged it to personal card and submitted in Concur. Is that ok?

tom (Finance): Per diem is meant to cover meals/misc, but we still allow laundry reimbursements on long trips as a separate actuals claim. Key rules: receipt required, must be reasonable, and satisfy the 7-night rule. If multiple laundry charges span >7 nights, we cap at $75 per 7-night block unless a manager pre-approves higher.

alina (People Ops): To clarify: if someone is on a 10-night trip, they can claim one 7-night cap ($75) plus an allowance for the remaining nights prorated. We usually prorate by nights: (75 / 7) * extra_nights rounded to nearest dollar. Example: 10 nights -> 75 + round((75/7)*3) = 75 + 32 = $107 cap. I'll add the math to the FAQ.

paul (Legal): Also confirm local tax treatment. In some jurisdictions laundry paid directly by company could create a taxable benefit. Finance should flag receipts from high-tax locations.

tom (Finance): Good point. If we pay vendor directly via AP or company card, Finance will assess taxability and include on payroll if required. If employee pays and claims, we usually reimburse net; employee is responsible for declaring if local law requires. We'll flag any reimbursed laundry >$200 for payroll review.

rachel (Engineering): The $65 was for dry-cleaning two shirts + trousers in London. I attached the receipt in Concur but got a question from approver. Does timing matter (i.e., laundry day within trip)?

alina (People Ops): Yes timing matters: expense must fall within the trip dates. If laundry was done before/after trip, it won't qualify. Also vendor name/address and total amount must be on the receipt. If receipt is digital with no itemization, a bank/card transaction plus vendor confirmation email is ok.

people-ops-bot: Submission checklist: 1) Trip dates match; 2) Original itemized receipt or vendor email; 3) Reasonable amount; 4) Mark as "Laundry - Long trip" category in Concur.

tom (Finance): For bulk laundry billed by an apartment host (e.g., weekly service on invoice), include the line item or vendor attestation. If host provides a lump sum with no breakdown, ask for a short email confirming amount allocated to laundry.

alina (People Ops): Action items: Tom will confirm tax thresholds for UK/DE/FR locations; Paul will draft short FAQ blurb on taxability; I'll update travel policy doc with prorate example and submission checklist. Rachel: your $65 claim looks fine if dates match.

rachel (Engineering): Thanks everyone. I'll add the landlord's laundry line item and resubmit. :thumbsup:
